A federal judge, Mark Pittman, is asking to be informed about any agreement that may have led a Musk-owned company to drop its antitrust allegations against Apple. Here are the details.

Judge seeks any deal reached with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple, with the dismissal being final. The lawsuit was one the two companies filed against Apple and OpenAI last year.

According to the initial complaint, Apple and OpenAI were accused of colluding through an agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence, thereby preventing other competing AI applications from gaining visibility on the App Store. Both Apple and OpenAI have denied the allegations.

In filings made earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI only stated that they had "reached a settlement regarding the allegations against Apple in this case," while emphasising that they were not seeking to withdraw the allegations against OpenAI.

According to POLITICO, which first reported the news, Judge Mark Pittman, who is presiding over the case, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit to the court "any agreement or combination of agreements reached with Apple concerning the resolution of the plaintiffs' claims against Apple in this lawsuit."

The ruling was made in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI. OpenAI demanded that X and SpaceXAI be compelled to disclose the agreement they reached with Apple to settle the dispute. Pittman also ordered the relevant companies to respond to OpenAI's motion by noon on September 17.
